title: Content security policy allows scripts from any host
description: A script-src directive that names a wildcard source appears in the response body. A wildcard source lets any host supply script, so an injected tag or a compromised third party runs with the page's origin no matter what the allowlist was meant to say.
remediation: Name the exact hosts the page needs and drop the wildcard.
limitation: One response body, first 32,768 bytes. It matches a wildcard source in the script directive; it cannot tell whether the value behind the marker is live or whether the page needs authentication.
scopeT: A response body that carries a script-src directive that names a wildcard source.
fp: A policy that names explicit hosts is not reported.
recordDesc: A script-src directive that names a wildcard source in a response hands every reader the view the build or admin side kept: A wildcard source lets any host supply script, so an injected tag or a compromised third party runs with the page's origin no matter what the allowlist was meant to say.
applicability: Deployments that render a script-src directive that names a wildcard source into a customer- or partner-facing response.
risk: A wildcard source lets any host supply script, so an injected tag or a compromised third party runs with the page's origin no matter what the allowlist was meant to say.

fix: Name the exact hosts the page needs and drop the wildcard.
